candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care → Advocacy/Client Rights/Case Management/Continuity of Care: provide and clarify information, support informed decisions, coordinate referrals and interprofessional care, and respect client preferences in treatment planning.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — education, advocacy, and coordination for kidney-care treatment decisions
candidate.educational_objective: Support informed kidney-care decisions through client/family education, advocacy, assessment, and interprofessional coordination rather than selecting the treatment modality for the client.

options.A: Assess the client's and family's needs, provide understandable education about available treatment approaches, support informed preferences, and coordinate questions and referrals with the interprofessional kidney-care team.
options.B: Select the treatment modality for the client because specialty nurses determine which option best fits the client's values and goals.
options.C: Limit nursing involvement to scheduling dialysis appointments because treatment education, advocacy, and transplant or conservative-care discussions are outside nephrology nursing practice.
options.D: Delay education until dialysis has already started because nephrology nursing is limited to clients receiving hemodialysis.

candidate.rationale: The American Nephrology Nurses Association describes nephrology nursing as care across acute and chronic kidney disease, dialysis therapies, transplantation, conservative management, and palliative/supportive care. ANNA identifies nephrology nurses as patient teachers, advocates, and coordinators who collaborate with the interprofessional team, help clients obtain information, support informed consent and treatment decisions, and promote client-desired independence. Therefore, A best reflects the specialty role. B substitutes the nurse's decision for the client's informed preferences, while C and D incorrectly restrict nephrology nursing to administrative or hemodialysis-only functions.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports nephrology nursing responsibilities for education, advocacy, informed treatment decisions, and interprofessional care coordination across the kidney-disease continuum.
candidate.source_document_title: The Nephrology Nursing Specialty; Nephrology Nursing Scope and Standards of Practice, 9th Edition
candidate.source_locator: ANNA 'The Nephrology Nursing Specialty' → Background/Roles/Practice Settings/Qualifications: nephrology nurses care across acute and chronic kidney disease and modalities including hemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis, transplantation, home therapies and conservative/palliative care. Role description: the nephrology nurse coordinates patient care with other team members and acts as patient teacher and advocate, assists the patient in seeking information, assures opportunity for informed consent in treatment decisions, and promotes patient-desired independence. ANNA Publications identifies the 2022 9th edition Scope and Standards as the current practice-scope resource.
candidate.source_version_date: ANNA Scope and Standards 9th edition 2022; current ANNA specialty page accessed 2026-08-18
candidate.stem: A client with advanced chronic kidney disease is beginning to consider kidney-replacement and conservative-care options. Which action best reflects the nephrology nurse's role?
